text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Justice Minister Frank Jensen has apologised for his intervention with regional officials over his brother's divorce, thereby fending off a parliamentary enquiry.

--Annual Danish beer sales fell to 121 litres per person in 1996 from 124 in 1995, while soft drink consumption rose to 93 litres from 90 and milk sales rose to 97 litres in 1996 from 93 the year before.

--The state's compensation bill for illegal deductions of labour market tax between 1988 and 1991 is now likely to be around one billion crowns, rather than 700 million as previously estimated, as more claims than expected are being filed.
--Mortgage lender Nykredit made about 500 million crowns from the sale of its shares in BG Bank after plans for a merger were dropped.
--The state earned close to three billion crowns in tax and duties from North Sea oil and gas production.
--State-owned Dansk Olie and Naturgas is investing in a new North Sea gas pipeline and in development of new fields.
--Farmers are expected to invest eight billion crowns in new buildings, equipment and stores in 1997, 1.25 billion more than in 1996.
--Den Danske Bank and Unibank are the only two to win approval as market-makers on the FUTOP derivatives exchange.
